# Learnings and mistakes

No structural facts are generated for this page; the store has no concept of a mistake, only of records, decisions and handovers. Everything here is written by hand.

## Notes (human, preserved verbatim on regeneration)

<!-- bm-human:begin -->
THE PATTERN, worth more than any single fix. A CHECK THAT CANNOT REACH AN ACTIONABLE VERDICT READS TO A PERSON AS A CHECK THAT PASSED, because the summary line says zero failed. Six instances, each found separately before anyone saw the shape:
1. The install identity check could only ever SKIP, and NOT because the installer was broken. scripts/install.py always wrote the stamp correctly. Every fixture in tools/test_install.py copied the tree with git history ignored, so the stamp was always "unknown". The tests that existed to prove the control worked were what silenced it.
2. The purge test pinned a dictionary by full equality, which catches a table ADDED to the purge and can never catch one FORGOTTEN. Forgotten is the direction data leaks through.
3. Three defects on the P0 problems page had already been fixed. The page kept sending readers to fix them.
4 and 5. Two guards enforced from a rendered page that the database does not back.
6. A lint reports roughly 150 hits with a sampled true-positive rate near zero, so nobody acts on it and a real one would hide among them.

MISTAKES THIS SESSION MADE, kept because the corrections are the evidence.
- Ran the full gate on a DIRTY tree. Its dirty-tree guard then attributed my own uncommitted files to the suites and printed something false about them. Run the gate on a committed tree.
- Ran the gate WITHOUT --artifacts, so two suites' failure text was never written to disk and the reason had to be recovered by re-running. Always pass --artifacts.
- Pushed a commit that turned three suites red. Not one failure was about the feature: all three were registries two new command line verbs had to join. The PO-6 rule covering exactly this had been forwarded to another agent an hour earlier by this same session. Knowing a rule and applying it are different acts.
- Folded a patch with `git apply` through Bash, which the fence hook does not gate, and so crossed a live fence unrefused. Refused on Edit, unrefused on shell, detected only afterwards. That gap is documented in this product's own limits page and now has a commit sha attached.
- Claimed BrotherSBE verification is read-only and safe against a contended tree. It is not: `sbe verify` mints evidence receipts. Asserted a property of a tool instead of checking it.
- Wrote a close report whose headline said DONE AND VERIFIED while its own later section admitted the battery had not run at the current tip. Caught by a drift check, not by care. Bind a verdict to a sha.
- Two agents were corrected by direct verification: one claimed the product's controls were inert on the real install shape, refuted by this session's own hooks having fired; one proposed building a check that already existed.

NEAR MISS WORTH KEEPING. A peer session was told by a scope reconciler that this session's in-flight work was out of scope, and offered three recoveries: restore would have deleted 111 lines of live work, declare would have filed a false ownership record, break glass would have required naming an approver who was asleep. It refused all three and messaged the owner instead. No tool prints the correct option; it had to be invented.
